newsitem.title: USA: Ill. Superconductor rejects shareholder proposals.
newsitem.headline: Ill. Superconductor rejects shareholder proposals.

text.p: Illinois Superconductor Corp said Monday its board of directors rejected shareholder Sheldon Drobny's proposals that the entire board resign with the exception of chairman and chief executive Ora Smith.
Drobny had also proposed Smith be replaced by Semir Sirazi as chief executive. Sirazi currently serves as vice president of 3Com Corp's Cable Access Business.
Illinois Superconductor called the proposals "self serving and not in the best interest of all stockholders".
The company said the board considered the proposals at its regularly scheduled meeting held today. It said Drobny had been invited to discuss his proposals but did not appear.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, Drobny, who owns a 7.7 percent stake in Illinois Superconductor, proposed replacing the board with Shan Padda, Stewart Shiman and Sirazi. He also called for an amendment to the shareholder rights plan to exclude common stock owned by himself, Shiman and Drobny's partner, Aaron Fischer.
"Such an amendment would have allowed Drobny to gain control of the company without paying a premium to its other stockholders," Illinois Superconductor said.
Drobny said last week he had no doubts in the company's technology but said it was time for the company to switch to a marketing mindset from a developmental focus.
Illinois Superconductor provides high-temperature superconducting technology for the wireless telecommunications industry.
